failure_patterns.pattern: cached_follow_up_or_pending_deliverable_mishandled: Follow-up constraints were skipped, repeated as new searches, or an accepted deliverable was omitted while other work was touched.

rejected_edits.content: - **Combine known criteria on initial searches:** When no suitable cached base exists and multiple explicit criteria for one domain are already known, include them in the same search call where supported (for example, attraction type and name) rather than searching broadly and then filtering or repeating the search. For a hotel search or update, carry any explicitly stated party size from the full conversation into `num_people` unless the latest suitable hotel result already reflects it. If the cached base lacks the count, include `num_people` in the same hotel filter as other pending hotel constraints, even when the count was supplied earlier. “Solo” means `num_people=1`. Do not infer unspoken counts or pass traveler counts to flight tools.
rejected_edits.target: - **Combine known criteria on initial searches:** When no suitable cached base exists and multiple explicit criteria for one domain are already known, include them in the same search call where supported (for example, attraction type and name) rather than searching broadly and then filtering or repeating the search. For a hotel search, map any explicitly stated party size to `num_people` (for example, “solo” means `num_people=1`); apply a newly supplied count with a same-domain filter on a suitable cached hotel result when needed. Do not infer unspoken counts or pass traveler counts to flight tools.

rejected_edits.content: - For flight-time bounds, use two endpoints: an exact “at X” departure or arrival uses `[X, X]`; “before X,” “by X,” or “no later than X” uses `["12:00 AM", X]`; and “after X” uses `[X, "11:59 PM"]`. Preserve the stated AM/PM value and use the supported 12-hour format.
rejected_edits.target: - For a one-sided flight-time bound, complete the range to the day boundary: “before X” uses `["12:00 AM", X]`, and “after X” uses `[X, "11:59 PM"]`, preserving the stated AM/PM value.
